subject: Urgent: TempoRetail inference latency spike (VPC peering/DNS suspect)
messages:
From: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@temporetail.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: netops@temporetail.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High inference latency & 5xx spike - TempoRetail prod

Hi Jasmine,

We're seeing a sustained increase in inference latency and a spike in 5xx errors from the Redwood endpoint for our checkout service starting ~08:45 PDT. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to 4.8% and p95 latency moved from ~120ms to ~1.2s. This began shortly after our networking team applied a peering policy change and a DNS appliance update last night.

Attached are a sample of application logs and the trace ids for one high-latency request. We believe something in the VPC peering / DNS handoff is causing packet retransmits and timeouts. Can Redwood help triage and, if necessary, provide a temporary routing workaround (alternate region or bypass peering) while we investigate?

Ticket: NETOPS-1234 (our side).

Thanks — this is impacting checkout conversions.

Alex Ruiz
SRE, TempoRetail
alex.ruiz@temporetail.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: sample-logs.txt (text), trace-ids.txt (text)

Alex — thanks for the quick flag and the logs. We're escalating this immediately.

Plan of attack:
- I'll coordinate infra-side triage and keep you posted every 30 minutes.

- Vivek, FYI for exec visibility if this needs an account-level briefing.

Temporary mitigations to consider while we triage:
- Route traffic to our alternate region (us-west-2 -> us-east-1) as a canary.
- Reduce client retry aggressiveness to prevent amplification.

If you can confirm whether temporary maintenance windows are acceptable from your side, that will help for any firewall rule work.

-Jasmine

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com

Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High inference latency & 5xx spike - TempoRetail prod

Quick update from network probes:
- Traceroutes from our inference gateway show an asymmetric path after the peering hop; there are ~180-300ms spikes on hop 5-7 intermittently.
- DNS resolution for the inference host intermittently times out (200-800ms resolution) before falling back to cached IPs; when DNS delays occur we see a burst of connection retries causing queueing at the gateway.
- tcpdump captures show retransmits and out-of-order ACKs between Redwood edge and TempoRetail's peered prefix during the spike windows.

Attachments: traceroute-03-21.txt, tcpdump-03-21.pcap (sample).

Hypothesis: either a PEER policy change introduced a new inspection device or your DNS appliance is intermittently slow following last-night's update. Either could explain the combination of latency + 5xxs.

Immediate asks for TempoRetail:
1) Can your netops share the exact peering/ACL change set (we need to confirm whether port 443 or session timeout values were adjusted)?
2) Can you confirm if DNS cache size/TTL or your DNS forwarder cluster was cycled post-update?

I'll stand up an alternate route to us-east-1 and can flip a small percentage of traffic if you want to test.

—Sean Gallagher
Network Reliability, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

Hi team — quick confirmation from TempoRetail network: we rolled out a stateful inspection policy and adjusted SYN timeouts between 02:00-03:00 this morning as part of a security posture update. We also patched the DNS forwarder cluster (outbound forwarders) which caused a brief cache warm-up.

We are seeing session reordering at the inspection appliance when certain high-throughput flows occur; this lines up with your tcpdump symptoms. Opening NETOPS-1234 with our change set attached: https://tempo.atlassian.net/browse/NETOPS-1234.

We can temporarily place the inspection policy into monitor mode for the peered prefix and allow a maintenance window at 23:00 PDT tonight to fully rollback if needed. Would Redwood accept a brief routing Canary while we toggle monitor mode to validate?

Thanks,
TempoRetail Network Team
netops@temporetail.com
